# A refused bound marks its date field when only its time changed

Owned: agreed with Vega on #21727, whose three #21724 assertions move with it; not offered to contributors.

## Context

The timeline's editor (`Neo.timeline.EventEditor`, used by the scheduler and the Gantt) shows each bound as a date field and a time field (`startDate` / `startDate__time`, `endDate` / `endDate__time`). When it refuses a save, it marks the date field even when the person changed only the time, so the message sits under a field they did not touch. #21722's Out of Scope deferred "which field shows the error", and #21727 left it out because moving the mark changes where #21724's tests read the error.

## The Problem

Two refusals in `EventEditor#save()` pick their field without asking which sub-field changed:

1. An end before the start marks `getField(endDateField)`: the End date, always.
2. An owner refusal (`commitTimelineEdit` returning `{status: 'refused', message}`, such as the scheduler's minimum duration from #21724) marks `getField(keys[0])`, the first changed record field. `getChanges()` keys on record fields, so that is a date field.

Reproducer on `dev` `cca960d9cd`: `test/playwright/unit/scheduler/Container.spec.mjs` › "the editor below the minimum (#21722)" moves an end from 11:00 to 08:15 on the same day (a time-only change), and its three refusal tests assert the error on `endDate` and `startDate` (4 passed, 1.3 s).

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: "the field the person has to fix carries the error: the time field once its date is set, the date field otherwise." (`src/timeline/EventEditor.mjs`, the JSDoc of `validateBound`). `validateBound` follows it for a bound that does not parse; the two refusals in `save()` do not.

- `save()` holds both branches.
- `initialValues` keeps each bound as its joined date and time (`getDateTimeValue()`), keyed by the date field, so the date and time parts can be compared to what the editor opened with.
- Since #21727 a bound's date and time fields both place their message across the row (`errorPositionAbsolute`), so moving the mark from date to time needs no layout change.

## The Fix

One `EventEditor` method resolves the field to mark for a bound: its `__time` field when its date is unchanged and its time changed, else its date field. Both refusals call it; the owner refusal maps its record key to the bound first. Update #21724's three assertions to read the changed sub-field, and add an editor unit test for the end-before-start case at both granularities.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A refusal after a time-only change of a bound marks that bound's time field (`endDate__time` or `startDate__time`), and its date field carries no error.
- [ ] A refusal after a change of a bound's date marks its date field, as today.
- [ ] #21724's three scheduler assertions read the changed sub-field and pass.
- [ ] `validateBound`'s marks for a bound that does not parse are unchanged.

## Out of Scope

- Which bound an end before the start marks when only the start moved: the End, as today.
- The messages' wording.
- Labels above the fields at 390, which needs a width-responsive `labelPosition` the form family lacks (named on #21727).
